open_questions: Are the original City Hall marquee letters (the 'Welcome Milwaukee Visitors' sign from the opening credits) on permanent public display at the Milwaukee County Historical Society, or only brought out for tributes? Call 414-273-8288 before making it a dedicated stop.

Confirm Lakefront Brewery's tour still ends with the theme-song sing-along and the glove-on-the-bottle gag after the 2023 switch to cans (owner said it would; Civic Media reported the sing-along still happening in Jan 2026). Weekend tours usually sell out, so book on etix before Friday.
Confirm current streaming: Pluto TV (free) was the only listed US streamer as of Jan 2026. Paramount+ was not listed on JustWatch; check the Paramount+ app in case that changed.

Koz's Mini Bowl (2078 S 7th St), the duckpin dive where the Badger Bus 'Laverne & Shirley's Milwaukee' tour did its milk-and-Pepsi tasting, was listed for sale in Aug 2022 and still operating in Jan 2024; current status unverified, so it is left off the pilgrimage list.
Is the Badger Bus Tours 'Laverne & Shirley's Milwaukee' costumed bus tour ($69, 2020) still running? No 2026 dates found.
hook: Was Laverne & Shirley filmed in Milwaukee? Schlemiel, schlimazel... no. It was filmed on a soundstage in Hollywood. But Milwaukee has spent fifty years acting like it was, and honestly, the city has earned it.
filmed_here_truth: Laverne & Shirley was SET in Milwaukee (a basement apartment at 730 Knapp Street, the Shotz Brewery bottling line, Frank DeFazio's Pizza Bowl) but it was FILMED on Paramount Stage 20 at 5555 Melrose Avenue in Hollywood, right next door to Stage 19, where Happy Days was shooting. The only real Milwaukee footage is in the opening credits: the establishing shot of Milwaukee City Hall with its lit marquee reading 'Welcome Milwaukee Visitors' (a 1906 message board on the tower's south face, dismantled in 1988; the letters survive at the Milwaukee County Historical Society). Everything else in the credits, including the girls skipping down the street and dropping the glove on the bottling line, was shot in California; the 'Shotz' brewery never existed, though its name was a wink at Schlitz, 'the beer that made Milwaukee famous.' For Season 6 (fall 1980) the writers moved the girls to Burbank after automation ate their bottle-capping jobs, which conveniently let the show chase Hollywood storylines; ratings slid from No. 1 to No. 20 and never recovered.
history:
Laverne & Shirley started as a one-off: in a November 1975 Happy Days episode, Garry Marshall needed two 'sure thing' dates for Fonzie and Richie, so he cast his kid sister Penny Marshall and her friend Cindy Williams (the two had been hired as comedy writers at Francis Ford Coppola's Zoetrope). The audience went nuts, ABC ordered a spin-off, and the show premiered January 27, 1976. It hit No. 3 in its first season, No. 2 in its second, and was the No. 1 show in America for 1977-78 and 1978-79, pulling more than 50 million viewers a week at its peak.

The premise was quietly radical for prime time: two single, working-class women in 1950s Milwaukee, capping bottles on the Shotz Brewery line, sharing a basement apartment at 730 Knapp Street, eating at Laverne's dad's Pizza Bowl, and being pestered by the upstairs greaseballs Lenny and Squiggy. Laverne drank milk and Pepsi. Shirley slept with a stuffed cat named Boo Boo Kitty. Neither needed a husband to be the hero of the episode.

The theme, 'Making Our Dreams Come True' (written by Charles Fox and Norman Gimbel, sung by Cyndi Grecco), became a real radio hit, peaking at No. 25 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1976. It opens with a chant Penny Marshall brought from her Bronx childhood, a Yiddish-American hopscotch rhyme: 'Schlemiel! Schlimazel! Hasenpfeffer Incorporated!' The show ran eight seasons and 178 episodes, moved the girls to Burbank in 1980, lost Shirley in 1982, and signed off May 10, 1983.
synopsis: Laverne DeFazio (loud, Italian, armored in a monogrammed L) and Shirley Feeney (prim, hopeful, armed with a stuffed cat) are best friends, roommates, and bottle-cappers at Milwaukee's Shotz Brewery in the late 1950s. Each week they chase dates, raises, and a slightly better life while fending off their upstairs neighbors Lenny and Squiggy, Shirley's on-and-off boyfriend Carmine 'The Big Ragoo' Ragusa, Laverne's pizza-slinging father Frank, and their landlady Edna Babish. In Season 6 they pack up for Burbank, California, and the show follows them west.

cast.bio_fun: Born Carole Penelope Marshall in 1943, she grew up at 3235 Grand Concourse in the Bronx, the same apartment building that produced Neil Simon, Paddy Chayefsky, Calvin Klein, and Ralph Lauren. Her big brother Garry created Happy Days and put her on it; the cursive L she wore came from a vintage sweater she spotted in the Paramount wardrobe department, and it is carved on her headstone.
cast.after_the_show: Became one of the most successful directors in Hollywood: Jumpin' Jack Flash (1986), Big (1988, the first film directed by a woman to gross over $100 million in the US), Awakenings (1990, Best Picture nominee), A League of Their Own (1992), The Preacher's Wife (1996), Riding in Cars with Boys (2001). Married to Rob Reiner 1971-81. Died December 17, 2018, at 75.

image.credit: ABC publicity photo, 1976 (public domain) via Wikimedia Commons

cast.bio_fun: Before Shirley she was already a New Hollywood darling: Laurie Henderson in George Lucas's American Graffiti (1973, BAFTA nomination) and Ann in Coppola's The Conversation (1974). She auditioned for Princess Leia, lost to Carrie Fisher, and instead became half of the No. 1 show in America.
cast.after_the_show: Left two episodes into Season 8 in 1982 after Paramount demanded she work on her scheduled due date; she sued for $20 million and settled. Toured in Grease and Deathtrap (often with Eddie Mekka), made her Broadway debut in The Drowsy Chaperone (2007), wrote the memoir Shirley, I Jest! (2015), and reunited with Penny Marshall on Nickelodeon's Sam & Cat in 2013. She came to Milwaukee for the Bronze Fonz unveiling in 2008. Died January 25, 2023, at 75.

image.credit: ABC publicity photo (public domain) via Wikimedia Commons

cast.bio_fun: McKean and David Lander invented Lenny and Squiggy as acting students at Carnegie Tech in Pittsburgh years before the show existed, then honed them in the L.A. comedy troupe The Credibility Gap. Penny Marshall knew them and got the duo hired, pre-made, as the upstairs neighbors.
cast.after_the_show: Co-wrote and starred in This Is Spinal Tap (1984) as David St. Hubbins; Mr. Green in Clue (1985); Saturday Night Live cast member 1994-95 (at 46, then the oldest person ever hired); Best in Show (2000); an Oscar nomination for co-writing 'A Kiss at the End of the Rainbow' from A Mighty Wind (2003); and, to a whole new generation, the brilliant, tragic Chuck McGill on Better Call Saul (2015-18, 2022; Emmy nomination 2019).

image.credit: Kingkongphoto & www.celebrity-photos.com, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

cast.bio_fun: The nasal 'Hello!' that announced Squiggy's every entrance was Lander's own creation from his Carnegie Tech days with McKean. He later voiced the weasel Smart Ass in Who Framed Roger Rabbit (1988) and Thumper in A Bug's Life (1998).
cast.after_the_show: Diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 1984, he hid it for 15 years, went public in 1999, became a National MS Society goodwill ambassador, and wrote the memoir Fall Down Laughing: How Squiggy Caught Multiple Sclerosis and Didn't Tell Nobody (2002). He also worked as a Major League Baseball scout for the Anaheim Angels and Seattle Mariners starting in 1997 and owned a small stake in the Portland Beavers. Died December 4, 2020, at 73.

image.credit: ABC Television cast photo, 1976 (public domain) via Wikimedia Commons

cast.bio_fun: A song-and-dance man from Worcester, Massachusetts, Mekka was a Tony nominee for Broadway's The Lieutenant before he landed Carmine, the boxer-turned-crooner who was forever almost marrying Shirley. His tap and swing numbers were the show's secret weapon.
cast.after_the_show: Penny Marshall cast him in A League of Their Own (1992) as the bar patron who swing-dances with Madonna. He did Hairspray in Las Vegas, toured Grease with Cindy Williams, and played Tevye in Fiddler on the Roof (2010). Died November 27, 2021, at 69.

image.credit: Leslie Gottlieb, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

cast.bio_fun: Born Fivel Feldman in Brooklyn in 1913, he took his stage name from Foster Avenue and worked the nightclub circuit from the 1930s on, billed in 1950s comedy shorts as 'Brooklyn's Ambassador to the World.' He traded jabs with Cassius Clay on The Jerry Lewis Show right before the first Liston fight.
cast.after_the_show: Laverne's pizza-and-bowling-alley dad was his last big role; he played the Pizza Bowl owner from 1976 to 1982 and appeared in Bang the Drum Slowly (1973) before it. Died July 8, 1985, at 72.

image.credit: ABC Television cast photo, 1976 (public domain) via Wikimedia Commons

cast.bio_fun: A genuine MGM musical star (On the Town and Take Me Out to the Ball Game, both 1949, opposite Frank Sinatra and Gene Kelly) whose film career was derailed when her husband Larry Parks was blacklisted after testifying to HUAC. She came back on TV as Archie Bunker's liberal neighbor Irene Lorenzo on All in the Family (Golden Globe, 1974).
cast.after_the_show: Played the five-times-divorced landlady Edna for 97 episodes (1976-81), eventually marrying Frank DeFazio; when she left for a Broadway commitment the writers divorced them off-screen. Kept working into her 80s, including Becker (Emmy nomination). Died February 12, 2011, at 91.

image.credit: ABC Television cast photo, 1976 (public domain) via Wikimedia Commons

cast_photo.caption: The 1976 cast. Standing: Carole Ita White (Rosie), Phil Foster (Frank), Eddie Mekka (Carmine), Betty Garrett (Edna), Michael McKean (Lenny), David Lander (Squiggy). Seated: Penny Marshall and Cindy Williams.

fun_facts.fact: Lenny and Squiggy were a band before they were neighbors. McKean and Lander's 1979 Casablanca Records album 'Lenny and the Squigtones' features a guitarist credited as Nigel Tufnel: Christopher Guest, five years before This Is Spinal Tap. Peter Criss of KISS shows up as 'Ming the Merciless.' The single was 'King of the Cars,' which they performed in character on American Bandstand.

Only one shot in the whole series is really Milwaukee: the opening-credits view of City Hall with its tower marquee reading 'Welcome Milwaukee Visitors.' The sign was a 1906 message board (42-inch wooden letters, fifteen 25-watt bulbs each, a catwalk behind so workers could swap messages) and was dismantled in 1988. The letters now live at the Milwaukee County Historical Society, which has spelled out PENNY (2018) and CINDY (2023) in its river-facing windows when each star died.

There is a Bronze Fonz on the RiverWalk (unveiled August 2008, five minutes from the Riverside Theater) but no Laverne, no Shirley. Cindy Williams actually flew in for the Fonz unveiling. A local business leader floated a Laverne & Shirley statue during the pandemic; Williams and Penny Marshall's daughter were both 'all for it,' but the timing was wrong and it never got funded. Milwaukee, you have homework.

Lakefront Brewery has ended every tour since about 2005 with the whole room singing 'Making Our Dreams Come True' and one guest dropping a glove onto a passing bottle, exactly like the credits. Their old bottling line was salvaged Schlitz equipment, which fans nicknamed the 'Laverne and Shirley line.' When Lakefront went cans-only in January 2023 the line was sold to a buyer in Mexico City, but owner Russ Klisch promised: 'We'll still have the glove.'

Shotz was a fake brewery with a very real wink: the name is a play on Schlitz, 'the beer that made Milwaukee famous.' The girls' fictional address, 730 Knapp Street, is a real street on the lower east side and, in the 1950s, was an easy walk to the actual Schlitz plant. The show reinforced the blue-collar, beer-town stereotype so well that Milwaukee's own historians still grumble about it.

The L on Laverne's sweaters was an accident. Penny Marshall spotted a vintage monogrammed sweater in the Paramount wardrobe department and claimed it; the letter became so much a part of her that it is carved into her headstone.

Milk and Pepsi was a real Penny Marshall habit written into Laverne. The Badger Bus 'Laverne & Shirley's Milwaukee' tour served it to guests; the costumed guide's review: 'like a watered-down milkshake.'

Boo Boo Kitty, Shirley's stuffed cat, got its name because Cindy Williams forgot a line in rehearsal and blurted it out. Mego made Laverne, Shirley, Lenny, and Squiggy dolls, and Matchbox sold a Shotz Brewery delivery van.

The theme song was a legitimate hit: Cyndi Grecco's 'Making Our Dreams Come True' peaked at No. 25 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 13 on the Adult Contemporary chart in 1976, and went to No. 16 in Canada. Marshall and Williams also cut an album in character, 'Laverne & Shirley Sing' (Atlantic, 1976).

The feud was real. Marshall and Williams clashed on set for years before Williams, pregnant in 1982, was told to work on her due date; she walked two episodes into Season 8 and sued Paramount for $20 million. Penny soldiered on as solo Laverne for the final season. The two eventually made up and reunited on Nickelodeon's Sam & Cat in 2013.

Yes, there was a Saturday-morning cartoon: 'Laverne & Shirley in the Army' (ABC, 1981), in which the girls enlist and answer to Sgt. Squealy, a talking pig voiced by Ron Palillo (Horshack from Welcome Back, Kotter). It was later merged with Mork & Mindy and Fonzie into one hour-long block.

Happy Days and Laverne & Shirley were literally next-door neighbors: Happy Days shot on Paramount Stage 19, Laverne & Shirley on Stage 20. The two shows crossed over in the two-part 'Shotgun Wedding' (1979), which started on Happy Days and finished as the Season 5 premiere of Laverne & Shirley.

The show turned 50 on January 27, 2026, and Milwaukee celebrated like it was its own. Lakefront's Russ Klisch told Civic Media that the fist-in-the-air sing-along hits hardest with women who came of age when factory floors were not exactly welcoming: 'one of the few times you ever get to sing on a brewery tour.'

milwaukee_pilgrimage.name: The Bronze Fonz
milwaukee_pilgrimage.address: Milwaukee RiverWalk, just south of E Wells St (east bank), Milwaukee, WI 53202
milwaukee_pilgrimage.blurb: Same Garry Marshall universe, same fictional Milwaukee, and a five-minute walk from the Riverside Theater. Gerald Sawyer's life-size Fonzie (unveiled August 18, 2008; Visit Milwaukee raised about $85,000 for it) is the closest thing the city has to a Laverne & Shirley monument, and Cindy Williams was there for the unveiling. Give him two thumbs up, then ask aloud where Laverne is.
milwaukee_pilgrimage.why: The only Happy Days-universe statue in town; there is no Laverne or Shirley statue (yet).

image.credit: Milwaukee RiverWalk by Michael Barera, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (the statue itself is copyrighted, so Commons has no photo of it)

milwaukee_pilgrimage.name: Milwaukee City Hall
milwaukee_pilgrimage.blurb: This is it: the one real Milwaukee frame in the entire series. The 1895 Flemish Renaissance tower (Wisconsin's tallest building until 1973) opened every episode with its marquee blazing 'Welcome Milwaukee Visitors.' The sign is gone since 1988, but stand on the east side of the river by the Fonz, look north, and you are in the opening credits. Four blocks from the Riverside.
milwaukee_pilgrimage.why: The only location in the show that was actually filmed in Milwaukee.
milwaukee_pilgrimage.hours: Exterior anytime; lobby weekdays during business hours.

image.credit: Gillfoto, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

milwaukee_pilgrimage.name: Milwaukee County Historical Society
milwaukee_pilgrimage.address: 910 N Dr Martin Luther King Jr Dr (Old World Third St), Milwaukee, WI 53203
milwaukee_pilgrimage.blurb: The 1913 bank building on Pere Marquette Park is where the actual 'Welcome Milwaukee Visitors' letters from the opening credits ended up (City Hall gave them to the art school MIAD, which handed them here in 2012). Staff spelled PENNY in the river windows when Marshall died and CINDY when Williams did. Cheap, quick, and a legit piece of the show you can stand next to. Ask at the desk whether the letters are out.
milwaukee_pilgrimage.why: Holds the real sign letters seen in the opening credits.
milwaukee_pilgrimage.hours: Mon and Wed-Sat 9:30 AM-5:00 PM; closed Tue and Sun; Saturdays often close at 2:00 PM for private events. Admission $8 adults.

milwaukee_pilgrimage.name: Lakefront Brewery
milwaukee_pilgrimage.blurb: The closest you can get to the Shotz line. Since about 2005 every Lakefront tour has ended with the whole group belting 'Making Our Dreams Come True,' fists in the air, while one lucky guest drops a glove onto a passing bottle (now a can; the old Schlitz-salvaged bottling line was sold in 2023, but the glove and the song stayed). Comedians give the tours, you get four 8-oz pours and a pint glass, and the beer hall does a Friday fish fry with a polka band. Also home to the original Bernie Brewer chalet from County Stadium.
milwaukee_pilgrimage.why: The only place on Earth that re-enacts the Laverne & Shirley opening credits daily.
milwaukee_pilgrimage.hours: Tours Fri Oct 23: 12, 1, 2, 3, 5, 5:30, 6:30, 7 PM; Sat Oct 24: 12 PM-6 PM every 30 min; Sun Oct 25: 12 PM and 2 PM; Mon Oct 26: 5 PM and 6:30 PM. $13 Mon-Thu, $16 Fri-Sun, 50 min, 21+ or with a parent. Weekend tours usually sell out; buy on etix. Beer hall Fri-Sat 11 AM-9 PM, Sun 11 AM-5 PM, Mon 11 AM-9 PM.

image.credit: jgagnon, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

milwaukee_pilgrimage.name: Best Place at the Historic Pabst Brewery
milwaukee_pilgrimage.blurb: Shotz never existed, but this did: the 1800s Pabst brewery complex, the kind of cream-city-brick beer castle the show was pretending to be. The hour-long Beer History Tour ($14, includes a pint) walks you through Captain Pabst's old offices and reception hall; the Blue Ribbon Hall tavern pours Pabst, Schlitz, and Blatz under a mural ceiling. Bonus for her dates: Haunted Pabst Brewery flashlight tours run Sunday Oct 25 and Monday Oct 26 at 6:00 and 7:30 PM ($20, includes a tallboy).
milwaukee_pilgrimage.why: The real brewery-baron Milwaukee the fictional Shotz was riffing on, plus the Schlitz brand still on tap.
milwaukee_pilgrimage.hours: Beer History Tour: Fri Oct 23 12, 2, 4 PM; Sat Oct 24 11 AM, 12, 2, 4 PM; Sun Oct 25 12, 2, 4 PM; Mon Oct 26 12, 2, 4 PM. $14 adults. Haunted tours Oct 25 and 26 at 6:00 and 7:30 PM, $20. Book at etix or 414-223-4709.

image.credit: Michael Barera, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

milwaukee_pilgrimage.name: Milwaukee Public Museum: Streets of Old Milwaukee
milwaukee_pilgrimage.blurb: A walk-through, lamp-lit replica of turn-of-the-century Milwaukee streets (cobblestones, a candy shop, Grandma peering out her window) that has been a rite of passage for every Milwaukee kid since 1965. It is the closest thing to a Shotz-era streetscape you can stroll, and this is your last chance: the Wells Street museum closes for good January 3, 2027, before moving to the new Nature & Culture Museum. Right now it is dressed up for 'Historic Halloween' through November 1.
milwaukee_pilgrimage.why: Last-chance nostalgia: the old-Milwaukee street set the show never had.
milwaukee_pilgrimage.hours: Wed-Mon 10 AM-5 PM, closed Tuesdays. Heads up: exhibit floors close at 1:00 PM on Saturday Oct 24 for a members-only event, so go Fri, Sun, or Mon. Adults $25 (includes a planetarium show).

image.credit: Sulfur, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

milwaukee_pilgrimage.name: 730 E Knapp Street (Laverne & Shirley's address)
milwaukee_pilgrimage.blurb: The girls gave their address as 730 Knapp Street, and Knapp Street is real: a quiet lower-east-side block of row houses and condos about a 12-minute walk northeast of the Riverside. There is no plaque, no basement apartment, and nothing was filmed here, which is exactly the point. Take the photo under the street sign, text it to someone with the caption 'Shirley, we're home,' and move on.
milwaukee_pilgrimage.why: The real street behind the fictional address.
milwaukee_pilgrimage.hours: Public street, anytime. Respect the residents.

where_to_stream.note: Pluto runs a dedicated Laverne & Shirley / Happy Days channel and had episodes on demand; as of January 2026 it was the only US streamer carrying the show.
Not listed on JustWatch as of this writing even though Paramount owns the show; worth a search in the app in case it has been added.
The complete series set exists if you are a physical-media person (about $60 on Amazon).

episodes_to_watch_in_the_hotel.title: The Society Party
episodes_to_watch_in_the_hotel.why: The pilot. Meet the apartment, the Pizza Bowl, Lenny and Squiggy's 'Hello!', and the whole premise in 24 minutes. Start here and the opening credits will be stuck in your head for the rest of the weekend.

episodes_to_watch_in_the_hotel.title: Excuse Me, May I Cut In?
episodes_to_watch_in_the_hotel.why: The dance-contest episode and a showcase for Eddie Mekka's footwork. The closest the show gets to a musical number, which fits a concert weekend.

episodes_to_watch_in_the_hotel.title: Guinea Pigs
episodes_to_watch_in_the_hotel.why: Broke and desperate for ball tickets, the girls sign up as paid medical test subjects. Peak physical comedy from Marshall and Williams and a fan favorite.

episodes_to_watch_in_the_hotel.title: Shotgun Wedding: Part 2
episodes_to_watch_in_the_hotel.why: The Happy Days crossover. Fonzie, Richie, and the gang land in Laverne & Shirley's world (Part 1 aired on Happy Days). Watch it, then go visit the Bronze Fonz with context.

episodes_to_watch_in_the_hotel.title: Not Quite New York
episodes_to_watch_in_the_hotel.why: The episode that ends Milwaukee: the girls lose their Shotz jobs to a bottle-capping machine and leave for Burbank. Poignant, a little bitter, and the moment the show stops being about this city.

the_chant.meaning: Three words of Yiddish and German nonsense that Penny Marshall carried from her Bronx childhood, where kids chanted it as a hopscotch rhyme. A schlemiel is the klutz who spills the soup; a schlimazel is the poor soul it lands on (mazel means luck, as in mazel tov). Hasenpfeffer is a German peppered rabbit stew. 'Incorporated' means nothing at all, which is what makes it perfect. Say it on the count of five, hook arms, and skip. Milwaukee will understand.
